ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the diagram, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\tan A= \frac{1}{2}$, D is a point on AC, and $\angle CBD=\angle A$. Then, what is the value of $\cos \angle CDB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[
\text{Solution:} \quad \because \angle CBD=\angle A,
\]
\[
\therefore \tan\angle CBD=\tan A=\frac{1}{2},
\]
\[
\text{Let } CD=a,
\]
\[
\therefore \tan\angle CBD=\frac{CD}{BC}=\frac{1}{2},
\]
\[
\therefore BC=2a,
\]
\[
\text{In } \triangle CBD,
\]
\[
BD=\sqrt{CD^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{a^2+(2a)^2}=\sqrt{5}a,
\]
\[
\therefore \cos\angle CDB=\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{a}{\sqrt{5}a}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}.
\]

From the text use ∠CBD = ∠A and tan A = 1/2, hence tan∠CBD = 1/2. In right triangle CDB, tan∠CBD = CD/BC, so set CD = a and BC = 2a. Then compute BD by the Pythagorean theorem: BD = sqrt(a^2 + (2a)^2) = sqrt(5)a. Finally, cos∠CDB = adjacent/hypotenuse = CD/BD = a/(sqrt(5)a) = sqrt(5)/5.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the diagram, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\tan A= \frac{1}{2}$, D is a point on AC, and $\angle CBD=\angle A$. Then, what is the value of $\cos \angle CDB$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \[ \text{Solution:} \quad \because \angle CBD=\angle A, \] \[ \therefore \tan\angle CBD=\tan A=\frac{1}{2}, \] \[ \text{Let } CD=a, \] \[ \therefore \tan\angle CBD=\frac{CD}{BC}=\frac{1}{2}, \] \[ \therefore BC=2a, \] \[ \text{In } \triangle CBD, \] \[ BD=\sqrt{CD^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{a^2+(2a)^2}=\sqrt{5}a, \] \[ \therefore \cos\angle CDB=\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{a}{\sqrt{5}a}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}}. \]
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is above, and triangle ABC has a right-angle mark at C; D is located on segment AC, and segment DB is drawn from D to B. Therefore CD is collinear with AC, and CB is perpendicular to AC, so triangle CDB is also right-angled at C. Reasoning: It is known that \angle CBD=\angle A, and \tan A=\frac{1}{2}, so \tan\angle CBD=\frac{1}{2}. In right triangle CDB, for angle \angle CBD, the tangent value is the ratio of the opposite side CD to the adjacent side BC, that is, \tan\angle CBD=\frac{CD}{BC}=\frac{1}{2}. Let CD=a, then BC=2a. By the Pythagorean theorem, BD=\sqrt{CD^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{a^2+(2a)^2}=\sqrt{5}a. It is required to find \cos\angle CDB. In triangle CDB, the adjacent side of angle CDB is CD, and the hypotenuse is BD, therefore \cos\angle CDB=\frac{CD}{BD}=\frac{a}{\sqrt{5}a}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}.
